newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arabs clash with Israeli police over tunnel.
newsitem.headline: Arabs clash with Israeli police over tunnel.

text.p: Police fired rubber bullets and teargas to disperse a stone-throwing protest by hundreds of students on Wednesday against Israel's opening of a tourist tunnel near an Islamic shrine, witnesses and police said.

The protest, on the northern outskirts of Jerusalem, and others outside Jerusalem's walled Old City and in Hebron and Nablus in the West Bank, were called by Yasser Arafat's Palestinian Authority in protest at the tunnel.

Palestinian hospital officials said seven people were treated for various injuries in the worst violence at a checkpoint near Ramallah in the West Bank, north of Jerusalem. Police said they fired rubber bullets to break up the protest.
Youths also scuffled with police outside the Damascus Gate entrance to walled Old Jerusalem.
Workmen on Tuesday opened a second entrance to the tunnel, igniting Palestinian charges that Israel was violating the religious status quo in the city holy to Moslems and Jews.

Witnesses said hundreds of students also hurled stones and bottles at Israeli troops in Hebron in the West Bank but no one was hurt. Thousands of students took part in a protest meeting called during a two-hour cancellation of classes at al-Najah university in Nablus, witnesses said.
